memos.headline: S08 leads the tape near 52-week highs; S02 and S07 break down on relative strength
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S08 is the standout leader—up +8.0% over four weeks, +14.7% over twelve, sitting just 1.2% off its 52-week high with an RSI of 64.3 and relative strength vs SPY of +8.1% over four weeks and +10.8% over twelve. S04 also impresses on a 12-week basis (+35.1%) with strong relative strength (+31.2% vs SPY over 12w), though its 4-week momentum has cooled and it sits 8.9% off highs, so I have slightly less conviction there. On the weak side, S02 is deeply oversold at RSI 36.9, trading 6.8% below its 50-day mean and down 7.1% over twelve weeks with -11.0% relative strength vs SPY—this is a broken trend until it reclaims the 50-day. S07 is the worst relative performer in the group at -22.5% vs SPY over 12 weeks and 24% off its high; I would avoid until it can hold above its 200-day mean. I'm neutral on the middle-of-the-pack names (S10, S06, S09) that show decent longer-term trends but lack near-term catalysts in price.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe: near 52w highs, +17.4% above 200d, RSI 64 not yet overbought, and dominant relative strength; would reassess on a close below 320 (roughly the 50d mean).
Exceptional 12w return of +35.1% and +31.2% relative strength vs SPY over that period, but 4w momentum fading and 8.9% off highs tempers conviction; a break below 465 would concern me.
Healthy uptrend (+12% above 200d, +7.8% rel strength 12w) but middling RSI and only 2.5% 4w return suggest no urgency; watching for a breakout above the 52w high near 236.
RSI 44.4 and slight negative 4w return suggest a pullback within a longer uptrend (+9.1% above 200d); needs to hold the 200d mean area to stay constructive.
Strong 12w relative strength (+15.6% vs SPY) but 4w return is -1.6% and momentum is stalling near the 50d; I'd wait for a fresh breakout above 171.
RSI 36.9, -6.8% below 50d mean, -7.1% over 12w, and -11.0% relative strength vs SPY—classic breakdown; would reconsider only on a reclaim above the 50d mean (~405).
Down 24% from 52w high, -18.6% over 12w, worst relative strength in the group at -22.5% vs SPY; trend is broken and I'd need a sustained move above 840 (50d area) to revisit.
Flat on both the 50d and 200d, negative 12w and 26w returns, and -7.6% relative strength vs SPY over 12w—no trend to follow in either direction.
Bouncing short-term (+3.3% 1w) but still 13.2% off highs and -2.6% relative strength over 12w; needs to clear 365 to confirm a trend change.
Sitting right at the 50d mean with RSI 48 and negative 4w momentum; longer-term trend is intact above the 200d but near-term direction is unclear.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 and S01 Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names with durable, expanding earnings power and those suffering margin erosion. S10 stands out with 106% YoY revenue growth, a 62% net margin, and $59.7B in net income on only $33.4B of total debt—this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S05 is similarly exceptional: 93.7% net margin, 24% revenue growth, and near-zero leverage at $14.8B debt, though the margin level invites scrutiny on sustainability. On the other end, S09 posted just 4.9% net margin with net income down 46% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth, and S01 saw net income decline 16% YoY on only 1.5% revenue growth with a 14.4% margin and $29.3B in debt against $21.2B in revenue. I would need to see S09's Q2 filing and any margin recovery before reconsidering; for S01, a return to positive earnings growth would change my view.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY with 62% net margin and modest $33.4B debt is the best earnings-power profile in the universe.
93.7% net margin and 298% YoY net income growth with minimal leverage is extraordinary, though margin sustainability warrants monitoring.
Full-year 10-K shows 39.7% net margin, 17.7% revenue growth, and 31.3% net income growth with manageable $40.3B debt—durable compounder.
$200.6B revenue with 19.6% growth and 245% net income expansion to a 31.2% margin is compelling, though $133B debt is elevated.
24% revenue growth and 65% net income growth with a 17.5% margin show improving operating leverage, but $36.2B debt on $20.5B revenue needs watching.
Strong 27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% margin, but $460.5B in total debt is an outsized liability that compresses equity returns if rates stay elevated.
Solid 16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% margin, but $82.3B debt and decelerating growth versus peers keep me at market-weight.
Revenue essentially flat at +0.4% YoY with a thin 4.9% net margin; 61% net income growth is off a depressed base and $73.3B debt is heavy.
Net income down 46% YoY to a 4.9% margin on barely growing revenue signals cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Revenue growth of just 1.5% with net income declining 16% and debt-to-revenue above 1.3x points to eroding earnings power.

memos.headline: Fed Pausing at 4% While 10y Yields Surge to 5%: Stagflationary Tilt Favors Defensives Over Duration
memos.body: I see a regime that has shifted from easing to pausing with a stagflationary lean. The Fed hiked the upper bound 25bp over the past three months to 4.00%, reversing the prior easing cycle that had cut 50bp over the trailing year, while CPI is running at 3.4% YoY with zero progress over the last three months. The labor market remains firm at 4.1% unemployment (down 20bp over 3m and 12m), which removes urgency for further easing but also means the economy is not cracking. The 10y yield at 5.01%—up 90bp YoY and 55bp in just three months—is the dominant signal: the term premium is repricing aggressively even as the 10y-2y spread flattens to just 27bp, suggesting the market is pricing persistent inflation and fiscal risk rather than growth optimism. A CPI print showing meaningful deceleration below 3% or unemployment rising above 4.4% would change my regime call from pause-with-hawkish-bias to renewed easing.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face severe headwinds with the 10y at 5.01% and rising 55bp in 3 months; discount rates are punishing long-duration cash flows.
Banks benefit from a pausing-to-tightening Fed, a positive (though narrow) yield curve, and firm employment supporting credit quality.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a stagflationary environment where inflation is sticky at 3.4% and rate volatility is elevated.
Energy is a natural inflation hedge but the labor market's resilience doesn't signal a demand boom; I stay neutral until clearer cyclical direction emerges.
Cyclicals face margin pressure from sticky inflation and rising borrowing costs with the 10y at 5%, and the flattening curve signals slowing growth expectations.
Without clear sector mapping I lean neutral; the macro backdrop of firm employment but rising rates creates offsetting forces.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S03 and S04 Momentum vs. S08 Weakness Persists Into September
memos.body: I see a clear sentiment split across the universe based on earnings-season price reactions and subsequent filing activity. S03 (+15.3%) and S04 (+15.5%) posted the strongest post-earnings pops in late July, and both have continued generating corporate event flow—S03 with a board change and an Other Events 8-K in September, S04 with an Reg FD disclosure—suggesting the positive narrative is being reinforced rather than fading. S08 stands out negatively: a -7.4% earnings reaction followed by a director departure/appointment amendment in September signals ongoing organizational turbulence that I do not think is fully discounted. S10 delivered a solid +8.7% earnings beat in late August and secured new financing, which reads as constructive momentum, though the "Other Events" filing on Sep 3 introduces mild uncertainty. S01's muted -1.9% earnings reaction combined with three simultaneous 8-Ks (including a management change and Reg FD) on the same day suggests a kitchen-sink quarter whose negative tone may already be priced.

views.note: Strong +15.3% earnings pop with continued positive event flow in September supports sustained bullish sentiment.
+15.5% earnings reaction was the largest in the universe and the Sep Reg FD disclosure keeps the narrative alive without negative signals.
-7.4% earnings drop plus a subsequent director change amendment suggests negative sentiment trajectory that may not yet be fully priced.
+8.7% earnings beat and new financing agreement point to improving tone, though the Sep 3 Other Events filing warrants monitoring.
+5.6% earnings reaction and a material definitive agreement in September suggest constructive but not exceptional momentum.
Mild -1.9% earnings dip with simultaneous management and Reg FD filings looks like a kitchen-sink reset; negative tone likely already absorbed.
Only a single Reg FD disclosure with no earnings reaction data gives insufficient signal to form a directional view.
One Other Events filing with no price reaction data provides too little information to gauge sentiment direction.

memos.headline: Surging Oil Prices and Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Supply-Chain Stress Across the Universe
memos.body: I am flagging a sharp divergence between equity-implied volatility (VIX at 15.44, still subdued) and the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, which has more than doubled in a month to 354 — a level historically associated with major sanctions or trade-policy shocks. WTI crude at $103.21, up 28% over three months, reinforces the picture of an energy-security disruption, likely tied to sanctions enforcement or supply-route risk. Credit spreads remain benign at 2.70% OAS, suggesting markets have not yet priced a sustained geopolitical shock into corporate credit, which makes me cautious rather than outright bearish. The 10y-2y spread compressing 26 bp in a month alongside the oil spike hints at a growth scare the bond market is beginning to discount. Without granular detail in the 8-K filings beyond item codes, I am relying on the macro signals to differentiate exposure: energy-linked and defense-adjacent names benefit, while consumer-facing and import-dependent names face margin risk from elevated input costs and policy uncertainty.

views.note: No company-specific filings to anchor a view; macro backdrop is mixed with low VIX but high policy uncertainty.
Recent 8.01 Other Events filing on Sep 14 coincides with the policy-uncertainty spike; without detail I stay neutral pending clarity on whether the event is geopolitically adverse.
Two 8-K filings in quick succession (Aug 17 and Sep 3) suggest active corporate communication, and if S10 has energy or commodity exposure the 28% oil rally is a tailwind.
Policy uncertainty doubling in a month raises tariff and export-control risk for import-dependent firms; the Aug 10 8.01 filing may reflect early supply-chain adjustments.
Twin Reg FD filings on Jul 29 are stale relative to the recent policy-uncertainty surge; I need updated disclosure before taking a directional stance.
Sep 8 Reg FD disclosure lands amid the sharpest one-month policy-uncertainty jump in the dataset; elevated oil costs and flattening yield curve suggest margin pressure.
Sep 2 Reg FD filing predates the worst of the uncertainty spike; credit spreads still calm but I would reassess if OAS widens above 3%.
